course.title: NumPy — From Beginner to Professional
course.description: A visual-first, practice-led NumPy course preserving the 220 numbered topics in the supplied 46-page curriculum PDF. It progresses from setup and ndarray fundamentals through indexing, broadcasting, statistics, random sampling, precision, linear algebra, FFTs, specialized data, file I/O, memory, testing, interoperability, specialist extensions, and applied workflows.
course.version_scope: Learning references checked against the official NumPy 2.5 stable documentation on 2026-10-13; the official news page listed NumPy 2.5.4 released 2026-10-10 as the latest patch at check time. An available execution environment here had NumPy 2.3.5, so code examples that were executed were observed under 2.3.5; review outputs and release notes before publication. NumPy 2.0 type-promotion and compiled-extension migration topics are explicitly included.
prerequisites: Basic Python syntax, variables, numeric types, lists, loops, functions, and importing modules. Basic arithmetic and algebra are helpful. No prior NumPy experience is assumed.
learning_outcomes: Create, inspect, index, reshape, combine, and manipulate multidimensional arrays.
Use element-wise operations, ufuncs, broadcasting, and vectorization with shape-aware reasoning.
Choose dtypes and handle casting, type promotion, overflow, non-finite values, and numerical tolerances deliberately.
Analyze data with statistics, sorting/searching, random sampling, probability distributions, linear algebra, polynomials, and FFTs.
Read/write numeric data safely and understand views, copies, strides, memory mapping, and performance trade-offs.
Write documented, reusable, typed, and tested NumPy functions that integrate with the scientific Python ecosystem.
Recognize specialist topics such as C API, F2PY, Cython, Array API interoperability, and compatibility maintenance.
Deliver reproducible applied projects with input validation, tests, documented assumptions, and clear output.
